questions.question: On the UN World Tourism Organisation definition, a tourist travels:
options: Outside the usual environment, for less than a year, for purposes not connected with earning money at the destination
Anywhere, for any length of time, for any reason
Only for leisure, never for business

questions.question: A visitor who arrives and departs on the same day is:
options: Not counted in tourism statistics at all
A day visitor or excursionist — counted, but spending a fraction of what an overnight tourist spends

questions.question: A Japanese couple's spending at the Table Mountain cableway is recorded as:
options: An import, because they will fly home
An export — inbound tourism earning foreign exchange inside our borders

questions.question: The MICE market refers to:
options: Medical, international, cultural and educational travel
Business tourism built on meetings, incentives, conferences and events

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY demand-side reasons for tourism's growth?
options: Rising real incomes, paid leave, longer healthier retirements, new middle classes
Jet aircraft, budget airlines, online booking

questions.question: On the supply side, the 'price of distance' collapsed because:
options: Jet aircraft and then budget airlines cut the cost of flying from a year's wages toward a week's

questions.question: South Africa's tourism hinge year was 1994 because:
options: The rand was strongest that year
The Kruger Park opened to the public
The end of apartheid and sanctions turned an isolated pariah into one of the world's fastest-growing destinations

questions.question: The 2020 pandemic taught which lesson about tourism?
options: Domestic tourism always replaces inbound losses
Tourism is a luxury spend with a fragile floor — world travel fell almost to zero in a quarter, silencing an industry carrying roughly one South African job in twenty

subtopics.title: What Tourism Does to an Economy

questions.question: Tourism's direct GDP contribution (about 3%) grows to 8 or 9% once indirect effects count, because of:
options: The multiplier — the lodge buys locally, workers spend wages locally, and each round of re-spending adds income

questions.question: Rand for rand, tourism creates more jobs than mining because it is:
options: Labour-intensive — beds, meals and guiding are produced by people, not machines

questions.question: The four beneficiary groups the syllabus names are:
options: Households, businesses, infrastructure and the state
Domestic, inbound, outbound and day visitors

questions.question: A leakage occurs when:
options: Too many tourists visit in one season
Foreign ownership, imported food and overseas-sold packages let much of each tourist rand exit before it can multiply locally

subtopics.title: South Africa's Profile, IKS and Policy

questions.question: South Africa's four product pillars are:
options: Scenery and wildlife; heritage and culture; events and business; climate
Beaches, casinos, malls and theme parks
Mining tours, farm stays, cruises and skiing
Aviation, rail, road and sea transport

questions.question: Indigenous knowledge systems count as a tourism asset because:
options: They are cheaper to run than game reserves
Tracking, healing knowledge, storytelling, craft and cuisine are products no competitor country can copy, earning where gate fees never reach
They replace the need for marketing

questions.question: The two policy duties attached to IKS tourism are:
options: Authenticity — communities own the telling — and benefit-sharing — communities bank the earnings

questions.question: The 1996 White Paper's division of roles states:
options: The private sector leads and government follows
Government leads, the private sector delivers, and communities must benefit

questions.question: Tourism is an INVISIBLE export because:
options: The buyer travels to the product, the foreign money stays, and the product never leaves the country
It is not recorded in statistics
Tourists cannot be seen at the border

questions.question: Your aunt from Mamelodi holidaying in Margate is:
options: Domestic tourism — rands circulating at home, feeding jobs but adding no new money

questions.question: The Canadian couple's one-week trip invoiced an airline, guesthouse, cableway, car hire, farm stall, restaurant, reserve and wine estate. The point is that:
options: One holiday feeds many industries at once — no container export does that on its way to the harbour
The couple should have booked a package

questions.question: The lodge's chef, guides and housekeepers form the:
options: Direct ring — jobs on the lodge's own payroll

questions.question: The farmer delivering vegetables and the village laundry form the:
options: Indirect ring — jobs in firms that sell to the lodge

questions.question: Lodge and supplier workers spending wages at the spaza, taxi and salon create the:
options: Induced ring — the multiplier wearing a lodge uniform

questions.question: The vehicle arrives full but the village stays poor when:
options: Ownership is foreign, food is trucked from afar and the package was paid overseas — the multiplying happened in someone else's economy

questions.question: Visitors buy the eleven-hour flight because of:
options: What exists only here — the Big Five in the wild, Table Mountain, Robben Island, the Cradle of Humankind, and living indigenous cultures
The cheapest beaches in the world

questions.question: The two rules that keep IKS tourism honest are:
options: Perform daily and charge in dollars
The community owns the telling, and the community banks the earnings
Use professional actors and imported crafts
Keep culture away from visitors entirely

questions.question: Which obstacle-fix pair is correctly matched?
options: Slow visas — extend e-visas to high-growth markets like China and India

questions.question: Keeping the lights on counts as destination marketing because:
options: A single service-failure video circles the globe faster than any marketing budget
